document.executive_summary: Verification of WO-04 confirms A's core finding: all four packages pass the client screen (quality 98/86/89/100 against the 80 floor; defects 1/5/1/5 against the ceiling of 5), and P1 is the unique lowest-energy qualifier at 6 kWh per acceptance batch. Successive gaps to P3, P2 and P4 are 8, 26 and 27 kWh; the winner-to-last spread is 61 kWh. A's recomputed margins and ratios match the trusted table. Two residual risks stand: P2 and P4 sit at the five-defect ceiling with zero spare slots, and all energy figures come from one shared acceptance batch. My independent ballot is P1.
document.figure_caption: Verification chart: energy per acceptance batch (P1 6, P3 14, P2 40, P4 67 kWh) on one linear scale, beside qualification margins; P2 and P4 sit at the zero-spare defect ceiling.

recommendation.rationale: P1 is the unique lowest-energy qualifier: 6 kWh against 14 (P3), 40 (P2) and 67 (P4), with quality 98, one defect and four spare slots. Its 0.06 kWh-per-quality-point ratio is best in field. Unverified cost or reliability data cannot override the measured energy minimum under the client's stated policy.

sections.body: Independent screen: quality indices read 98, 86, 89 and 100 against the 80 floor, giving margins of 18, 6, 9 and 20 points. Raw defect counts read 1, 5, 1 and 5 against the ceiling of 5. All four qualify; no exclusion applies. Because qualification is binary and all candidates pass, the energy-minimization rule alone decides the pick, and the lowest energy is unique so no ID tie-break is needed. P2 sits nearest the quality floor at 86, while P2 and P4 exhaust their defect allowance.
sections.heading: Eligibility Recomputation

sections.body: Energy ranks P1 6, P3 14, P2 40 and P4 67 kWh per identical acceptance batch. Successive gaps of 8, 26 and 27 kWh and the 61 kWh winner-to-last spread check out arithmetically. A's energy-per-quality ratios (0.06, 0.16, 0.47, 0.67) reproduce to two decimals from the trusted table. P4's quality index of 100 cannot offset drawing 67 kWh, because the policy is energy-first and quality only gates entry. The 26 kWh jump from P3 to P2 cleanly splits a low-energy pair from a high-energy pair.
sections.heading: Energy Ranking and Gaps Verified

sections.body: A's round-4 prose recomputes correctly: margins, gaps, ratios and energy-first logic all match the trusted table, and the summary correctly flags P4's five defects as exactly at the ceiling. Round 3 recorded figure errors (A's missing P2 bar; my own misordered bars). A's stated remedy — regenerate from the table at one linear scale with tabulated value labels — is the right control, and I apply the same discipline to my own chart here. The drawn bars in A's rendered figure should still be pixel-checked against the 6/14/40/67 table before sign-off.
sections.heading: Audit of A's Current Brief

sections.body: Measured facts: four quality indices, defect counts and energies, all on the shared acceptance basis. Open questions: batch-to-batch variance (one batch only), and cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability, which are unverified and cannot move an energy-first ranking. Sensitivity: P2 and P4 disqualify on any single added defect; P2 sits only six points above the quality floor. None of these open items changes the ranking under the stated policy, but they should be recorded in the next analyst's handover.
sections.heading: Facts versus Open Questions
